answer: Epoch-Linked Behavioural Anchor Rule. Each identity's actions are scored per epoch; a crystal record of its behavioural fingerprint is stored across a fixed horizon of prior epochs. New identities whose fingerprint fails to match a stable trajectory are throttled until consistency accrues. An attacker must maintain many distinct, persistent behavioural histories in parallel across the whole horizon, paying the full operational cost of sustained independent activity per sybil—cost that scales linearly and cannot be amortized.
